target: calyptra corolla (PO_0025330) present [petal|corolla]; calyptra calyx (PO_0025329) present [sepal|calyx]
reason: Calyptrate petals or calyx are fused into a cap that falls off as one piece; PO has calyptra corolla and calyptra calyx for exactly this. Calyptrate stipules and bracts (fused into a cap over the bud) are not covered by this rule and stay unannotated.
A tip that comes to a point that is not sharp but is not rounded either is the FLOPO definition of subacute. PATO:0002091 subacute is a process duration and must not be used.

A general impression that comes from different causes (plumose pappus bristles, many exserted stamens, woolly hairs). The cause is the quality to annotate; PATO:0104366 floccose needs hairs that rub off, which the floras do not say.

label: spathe-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a spathe: a large, bract-like structure that sheathes or encloses another structure and is often split down one side. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like, worded as they are; the spathe itself is FLOPO_0986007.
reason: A standard botanical term for a spathe-like calyx, leaf or stipule, found in 9 floras; bract-like does not include the sheathing, one-side-split form.
'Upper 3 stamens staminodial' means those stamens are staminodes (sterile stamens); the word names the part, not a quality of it.

label: thicket-forming
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of its many woody stems, often arising from suckers or rhizomes, growing close together into a dense stand. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991007 caespitose and FLOPO:0991010 mat-forming. The older candidate FLOPO_0980347 'dense thicket' sits under mass density and should be replaced by this class.
reason: A habit used in 9 floras with a clear meaning (woody, clonal, dense stand); caespitose is a tuft of herbaceous shoots and mat-forming is a flat mat on the ground.

'Petals all of equal length' is a quality of a set of like parts, which is FLOPO equal. 'Of the same length as the sepals' compares two parts and goes to pattern 10 (docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md).
'Style apically stigmatic' and 'proximal 1/2 stigmatic' say that the style or style branch bears a receptive stigmatic surface on that region; the region goes to the region-of-the-bearer pattern.
Ragged margins of sepals, stipules and leaves are irregularly cut as if torn, which is the definition of lacerate. 'Bark becoming ragged' is shredding bark and belongs to FLOPO:0991021 exfoliating.
Blackened anthers, leaf bases and stipes are black or turning black; 'blackened when dry' goes to pattern 06 (specimen condition).

label: pandurate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being fiddle-shaped: oblong to obovate, with a concave narrowing on each side below the middle. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991056 obcordate and FLOPO:0991024 ovate.
reason: A standard leaf-blade and labellum outline with no term in PATO or FLOPO; it is used in 9 floras.
Same as the rule for 'lenticular' (C202): lens-shaped fruits and seeds are biconvex. 'Plan-convexes' seeds go to FLOPO:0991184 plano-convex instead.
Apetalous means without petals. 'Apérianthée' means without a perianth and should be its own rule: perianth (PO_0009058) absent.

label: astringent
definition: A flavor quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's causing a dry, puckering sensation in the mouth, as from tannins. NOTE: PATO has only flavourful and flavourless under flavor; kept in FLOPO beside the odour values.
reason: A standard taste quality of fruits, pulp, leaves and seeds in 9 floras, with no PATO term; it is treated like the FLOPO scent values.

label: dioicous
definition: A reproductive quality of a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its male and female gametoecia being borne on separate individual plants. NOTE: The bryophyte counterpart of FLOPO:0991072 dioecious (seed plants); sibling of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous.
reason: 1126 moss statements. FLOPO dioecious is defined for seed plants and its review note asks to keep bryophyte usage apart, as was done for autoicous.
A spelling variant of gland-dotted, an existing FLOPO value.
Mostly moss leaf cells whose walls have pores (bearer: the cell, with the wall as its region). 'Anther dehiscence porose' should go to FLOPO:0991153 poricidal instead.
Veins joining one another, often in loops near the margin; the same meaning as anastomosing.

target: new: compound of hair orientation and pilosity (puberulous FLOPO:0991049 + appressed FLOPO:0991064 on the hairs)
reason: Two values run together: short hairs (puberulous) that lie flat (appressed). Strigulose would add stiffness, which the source does not state.
Carnose means fleshy. Compounds such as 'carnose-coriaceous' are a continuum between two values and go to that pattern.
Corniculate means bearing small horn-like projections, which is what FLOPO horned covers. 'Not corniculate' is its negation.
Galeate (helmet-shaped) is the hooded, concave shape of the upper sepal or corolla lip; glossaries treat it as hooded, and a separate helmet class would be hard to tell apart from it.
An ampliate corolla tube or leaf base is widened or enlarged; same reading as rule C181 'expanded'.

label: dolabriform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like the head of a hatchet: narrow at the base and widening into a broad, oblique, curved distal edge.
reason: A precise botanical shape for staminode limbs, petals and thecae, with no term in PATO or FLOPO. 'Dolabriform hairs' (hairs attached near the middle) is a different sense and must not use this class.

Bicolorous leaf blades have two surfaces of different colour, and bicolorous fern scales have a dark centre with pale margins; both are parts of one structure differing in colour, which is discolorous.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer): cell wall or capsule wall + inflexible (PATO_0001545)
reason: The quality belongs to the wall of the bearer, not to the cell or capsule as a whole. It is the wall region with 'firm' (read as stiff, as in rule C186 rigid), like 'thick-walled'.
Nutant means nodding: bending or hanging downward. The reviewed union pair 'erect or nodding' already maps nodding to drooping.
In anisophyllous plants the leaves of a pair or node differ in size, which is FLOPO unequal on the leaves. Statements about the whole plant move to the leaves.
Nitid means shining or glossy, which PATO glistening has as exact synonyms; same as rule C201 'lustrous'.
In monadelphous stamens the filaments are fused with one another, which is connate. The rule drops the 'single bundle' detail (the source words keep it); diadelphous would need a count.
